evidence.claim: Across Nebraska, an automobile trail follows a corridor shaped by railroads.
evidence.quote: The Lincoln Highway was gradually replaced with numbered designations after the establishment of the U.S. Numbered Highway System in 1926, with most of the route becoming U.S. Route 30 from Pennsylvania to Wyoming.

evidence.claim: Across Nebraska, an automobile trail follows a corridor shaped by railroads.
evidence.quote: It followed the Platte River route across Nebraska; ultimately, about half of its mileage was on the Union Pacific right-of-way.

evidence.claim: The Lincoln Highway Scenic & Historic Byway crosses Nebraska on US 30, a route the Nebraska Department of Transportation identifies as a National Scenic Byway.
evidence.quote: Lincoln Highway Scenic & Historic Byway (awarded National Scenic Byway) 400 miles along U.S. Highway 30

evidence.claim: Visit Nebraska presents the drive through the history of pioneers, cowboys and Pony Express riders, alongside cultural and natural attractions.
evidence.quote: experience the history of pioneers, cowboys and Pony Express riders—plus cultural and natural treasures

evidence.claim: At North Platte, US 30 follows the north side of the Platte and South Platte rivers; farther east, Columbus occupies flat river-valley ground with rolling hills to its north.
evidence.quote: U.S. Route 30 intersects with U.S. 83 downtown and follows the north side of the Platte/South Platte River from east to west.

evidence.claim: Carl G. Fisher conceived the Lincoln Highway in 1912, and it was dedicated in 1913 as a coast-to-coast automobile route from Times Square to Lincoln Park in San Francisco.
evidence.quote: Conceived in 1912 by Indiana entrepreneur Carl G. Fisher, and formally dedicated October 31, 1913, the Lincoln Highway runs coast-to-coast from Times Square in New York City west to Lincoln Park in San Francisco.

evidence.claim: The Lincoln Highway Association formed to plan, promote and sign it.
evidence.quote: The Lincoln Highway Association, originally established in 1913 to plan, promote, and sign the highway

evidence.claim: Numbered highways gradually replaced the named route after 1926, with much of it becoming US 30.
evidence.quote: The Lincoln Highway was gradually replaced with numbered designations after the establishment of the U.S. Numbered Highway System in 1926, with most of the route becoming U.S. Route 30 from Pennsylvania to Wyoming.

evidence.claim: Driving east, begin with Kimball and Sidney, then continue through Ogallala to North Platte. Gothenburg and Lexington lead onward to Kearney and Grand Island. Columbus and Fremont come before Blair at the eastern end of the tourism route.
evidence.quote: From Blair: 24 miles west on US-30 to Fremont • 49 miles west on US-30 to Columbus 63 miles west on US-30 to Grand Island • 39 miles west on US-30 to Gibbon 13 miles west on US-30 to Kearney • 41 miles west on US-30 to Lexington 19 miles west on US-30 to Cozad • 13 miles west on US-30 to Gothenburg 37 miles west on US-30 to North Platte • 34 miles west on US-30 to Paxton 21 miles west on US-30 to Ogallala • 72 miles west on US-30 to Sidney 21 miles west on US-30 to Potter • 21 miles west on US-30 to Kimball

evidence.claim: farther east, Columbus occupies flat river-valley ground with rolling hills to its north.
evidence.quote: It is built on the flat terrain of the Platte River valley; rolling hills rise to the north of the city.

evidence.claim: Cattle driven from Texas met the Union Pacific railhead at Ogallala.
evidence.quote: Ogallala first was founded as a terminus for cattle drives that traveled from Texas to the Union Pacific railhead located there.

evidence.claim: The railroad arrived in 1867, before the town was laid out in 1875 and incorporated in 1884.
evidence.quote: The Union Pacific Railroad reached Ogallala on May 24, 1867.  The city itself was not laid out until 1875 and not incorporated until 1884

evidence.claim: The cattle routes were known as the Western or Great Western trails.
evidence.quote: These trails are known as the Western or Great Western trails.

evidence.claim: In the post office is Frank Mechau’s oil-on-canvas mural Long Horns, painted in 1938.
evidence.quote: The Ogallala post office contains an oil-on-canvas mural, titled Long Horns, painted in 1938 by Frank Mechau.

evidence.claim: It belongs to the federal mural program run through the Treasury Department’s Section of Painting and Sculpture, later called the Section of Fine Arts.
evidence.quote: Murals were produced from 1934 to 1943 in the United States through the Section of Painting and Sculpture, later called the Section of Fine Arts, of the Treasury Department.

evidence.claim: A locomotive’s maintenance stop gave North Platte time to feed soldiers.
evidence.quote: The reason that the train stopped in North Platte was because the town was a designated tender point for steam trains.

evidence.claim: Crews lubricated wheels and replenished water while trains paused here.
evidence.quote: Stopping the train allowed for the train crews to relubricate the wheels, top off the water levels in the tanks, and other tasks for the maintenance of the locomotive.

evidence.claim: The North Platte Canteen operated from Christmas Day 1941 to April 1, 1946, offering refreshments during ten- to fifteen-minute stops.
evidence.quote: operated from Christmas Day 1941 to April 1, 1946.

evidence.claim: Volunteers came from more than 125 communities, and their groups supplied the day’s food.
evidence.quote: Over one hundred and twenty five communities donated their time to work at the canteen.

evidence.claim: The canteen continued serving troops returning home after the war.
evidence.quote: At the end of the war, the canteen continued to operate as men were returning home.

evidence.claim: The Lincoln County Historical Museum has a display telling its history.
evidence.quote: Lincoln County Historical Museum contains a display detailing the history of the North Platte Canteen.

evidence.claim: offering refreshments during ten- to fifteen-minute stops.
evidence.quote: its purpose was to provide refreshments and hospitality to soldiers who were traveling through the area on the way to war during their ten- to fifteen-minute stopovers.

evidence.claim: their groups supplied the day’s food.
evidence.quote: The groups also took responsibility in supplying food for the day.

evidence.claim: At Pawnee Park, bronze soldiers step from a life-size replica of a Higgins boat into sand.
evidence.quote: The Andrew Jackson Higgins National Memorial in Pawnee Park features a life-sized replica of a Higgins boat with bronze statues of soldiers exiting into the sand.

evidence.claim: Columbus was the birthplace of boat designer Andrew Jackson Higgins, the designer of the Landing Craft, Vehicle, Personnel, used in World War II.
evidence.quote: Columbus is the birthplace of Andrew Jackson Higgins, creator/designer of the Landing Craft, Vehicle, Personnel (LCVP or Higgins boat), used during World War II.

evidence.claim: The Andrew Jackson Higgins National Memorial includes sand from 58 historically significant beaches, including D-Day beaches and beaches in Korea and Vietnam.
evidence.quote: The memorial includes sand samples from 58 beaches of historic significance: D-Day beaches of World War II, and beaches in Korea and Vietnam.

evidence.claim: Another memorial on the same site extends the story beyond those wars: the Freedom Memorial incorporates steel from the World Trade Center, destroyed in the attacks of September 11, 2001.
evidence.quote: The site is also home to the Freedom Memorial, which incorporates steel from the remains of the World Trade Center, destroyed by terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001.

evidence.claim: Near Sidney, the landscape reaches the western edge of the wheat-growing region; farther west, cattle ranching takes a larger share of the land.
evidence.quote: Sidney is toward the western edge of the Midwestern wheat-growing region. West of the city, the land is increasingly used for cattle ranching.

evidence.claim: In Columbus, automobile traffic encouraged new garages and hotels, and the city paved and lit downtown streets to attract motorists.
evidence.quote: Traffic on the two transcontinental auto routes through and near central Columbus spurred a burst of commercial construction. Hotels were expanded and new ones built; service garages were opened. To make the route through Columbus more attractive to motorists, the city undertook to illuminate and pave the downtown streets.

evidence.claim: Blair lies in the Loess Hills, surrounded by rolling hills and the Missouri River valley.
evidence.quote: Blair is located in the Loess Hills, surrounded on all sides by rolling hills and the Missouri river valley.

evidence.claim: The South Platte runs through Ogallala, a town shaped by cattle trails and the railroad.
evidence.quote: The South Platte River runs through Ogallala.

evidence.claim: a town shaped by cattle trails and the railroad.
evidence.quote: Ogallala first was founded as a terminus for cattle drives that traveled from Texas to the Union Pacific railhead located there.

evidence.claim: After witnessing an impromptu welcome for troops, Rae Wilson proposed making the train greetings a regular undertaking.
evidence.quote: As she walked away from the train that evening, she had an idea to meet all the trains that went through North Platte and give the soldiers the same type of sendoff. The next day she suggested that the meeting of soldiers become a permanent occurrence.
